No additional incentives such as per-diem allowances or bonuses have been included to attract craft labor. • While not included at this time, labor incentives may ultimately be required to attract and retain skilled labor depending on the amount of competing work in the region and the availability of skilled craft in the area at the time the projects proceed to construction. • The estimates are based on a greenfield site. • The site is classified as Seismic Zone 1, relatively level, and free from hazardous materials, archeological artifacts, or excessive rock. Soil conditions are considered adequate for spread footing foundations. The soil-bearing capability is assumed adequate such that piling is not needed to support the foundation loads. • Engineering and construction management costs are estimated based on B&V’s historical experience in designing and building power projects. The cost, as a percentage of BEC, varies by technology but is assumed to be 20 percent for the study cases. This percentage was selected based on those used for NGCC power plants in the NETL Fossil Energy Baseline study (Turner, et al., 2025). These costs consist of all home office engineering and procurement services as well as field construction management costs. Site staffing generally includes construction manager, resident engineer, scheduler, and personnel for project controls, document control, materials management, site safety, and field inspection. 2.11.1.5 Price Fluctuations Prices of equipment and bulk materials fluctuate as a result of various market forces. Some reference quotes post-dated the 2023-year cost basis while others may be considered more historical. All vendor quotes used to develop these estimates were adjusted to January 2023 dollars to account for price fluctuations. Price indices such as the Chemical Engineering Plant Cost Index (Chemical Engineering, 2024), Producer Price Index, and Handy Whitman Index were used as needed for these adjustments. While these overall indices are nearly constant, it should be noted that the cost of individual equipment types may still deviate from the January 2023 reference point. 38 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 2.11.1.6 Process Contingency Process contingencies were applied to the plant cost estimates, with justification provided, as follows: • Shell ADIP-Ultra Pre-Combustion CO Capture System: 17 percent due to pre-combustion 2 capture processes operated at full size but not used commercial on a wide-spread basis. • Shell CANSOLV Post-Combustion CO Capture System: 18 percent due to post- 2 combustion capture processes operated at full size but not used commercial on a wide- spread basis. • Instrumentation and Controls: 5 percent on all accounts due to integration issues with the capture system 2.11.1.7 Owner’s Costs Detailed explanation of the owner’s costs is available in the 2024 revision of the QGESS document, “Cost Estimation Methodology for NETL Assessment of Power Plant Performance” (NETL, 2025b).
